title: Running a container with --userns=auto fails due to mappings not being found, even though they are present
body:
### Issue Description

Consider the following command:

```
sudo podman run --rm -it --userns=auto alpine:3 /bin/sh
```

And the following mappings:

```
# /etc/subuid
yorickpeterse:524288:655360
containers:2147483647:2147483648

#  /etc/subgid
yorickpeterse:524288:655360
containers:2147483647:2147483648
```

On Fedora 44, which uses Podman 5.8.9, the above command will work as expected. However, starting with Fedora 45 which uses Podman 6.2.0, the output is instead as follows:

```
ERRO[0004] Cannot find mappings for user "containers": no subuid ranges found for user "containers" in /etc/subuid 
Error: creating container storage: not enough unused IDs in user namespace
```

In this case no other containers are running on the system, so it's not a case of e.g. a container with `--userns=keep-id` hogging all the IDs:

```
$ sudo podman container ls --all
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE       COMMAND     CREATED     STATUS      PORTS       NAMES
```

I tried to look at the release notes and existing issues, but I'm unable to find any information as to why this command is no longer working in spite of the mapping for "containers" being very much present in the relevant files.

Note that this error also happens when running directly as the `root` user (e.g. by logging in as root), as I also observed this on my bootc-based servers (which launch the containers from the root user).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Ensure that `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` have a `containers:2147483647:2147483648` entry
1. Run `sudo podman run --rm -it --userns=auto alpine:3 /bin/sh`


### Describe the results you received

```
ERRO[0004] Cannot find mappings for user "containers": no subuid ranges found for user "containers" in /etc/subuid 
Error: creating container storage: not enough unused IDs in user namespace
```

### Describe the results you expected

The command works as expected, as it did with Podman 5.8.

comments.body:
can you show `podman info` when running as rootless?

What do you get with `podman unshare cat /proc/self/?id_map`?  If there is only one mapping active, can you try `podman system migrate` and try to create the container again?

sorry, nevermind my last, I've missed you are trying as root.

containers:2147483647:2147483648

That is not enough, you are just giving one additional ID, make the range larger; for both files.

> That is not enough, you are just giving one additional ID, make the range larger; for both files.

No? The format is name:id:count? So the range is uid+count so the given config should work fine.

The actual error is

> ERRO[0004] Cannot find mappings for user "containers": no subuid ranges found for user "containers" in /etc/subuid

And since you mention the f45 update the issue is that you do not have the cotnainers user created, the user must actually exists not just be a line in /etc/subuid, see https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/issues/1710 https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2555286

@Luap99 From what I could find the user never needed to actually exist, and indeed this was the case in the past. Is this a new requirement as of Podman 6.x? If so, then at the very least the manual page should be updated to clarify that as currently all it says is this:

```
     • rootful mode: The --userns=auto flag requires that the user name containers be specified in the /etc/subuid  and
       /etc/subgid  files, with an unused range of subordinate user IDs that Podman containers are allowed to allocate.
       Example: containers:2147483647:2147483648.
```

**EDIT:** OK reading through the issues linked it indeed appears to be a recent change, though the manual page could probably be clarified for this. If that makes sense I'll happily submit a PR for that.

It has nothing to do with the podman version, its about the libsubid lookup which requires this now, see the linked issue.

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/main/troubleshooting.md#44-sudo-podman-run---usernsauto-fails-with-cannot-find-mappings-for-user-containers
always documented to create the user FWIW

But sure PRs to update the manpage welcome. Technically speaking when podman is compiled with libsubid then the mappings do not even have to come from /etc/subuid file. nsswitch.conf could be configured to load it from somewhere else, i.e. a central network user db.
@Luap99 thanks I wasn't aware of this new behavior and the error is not clear, opened a PR: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1380
